schemaNote: BSV teleop recipe v0.1 (draft format, original BSV material). Not an official NVIDIA procedure.
title: SO-101 simulation practice session
statusNote: Written by BSV from the curriculum below; BSV has not run this procedure in Isaac Lab or Isaac Teleop. Follow NVIDIA's current official instructions wherever they differ.
notIncluded: Controller mapping and retargeting settings: they depend on your input device and the official task id, so record the ones you used instead of copying a preset.
Real-hardware steps: this recipe is simulation only. Real-hardware authority belongs to the hardware owner or partner.

before: Note the Isaac Lab and Isaac Teleop versions (or source revisions) and the official task id you will run.
Launch the task, confirm the input device moves the simulated follower, and run one reset before recording.
Decide the session goal (attempted episodes, time box) and write it in the session note.
during: Record every attempted episode, including failures; do not delete failed episodes.
Label each episode right after it ends: SUCCESS, FAILURE or PARTIAL, and a failure category when it is not a success.
Reset between episodes using the documented reset path; note any reset that did not return the scene to its start state.
Stop the session if the simulator becomes unstable, and note it as a safety/reset event.
after: Count attempted, successful and failed episodes and episodes that needed recovery.
Review at least one failed episode and write one concrete change for the next session.
Build the session evidence and practice record on the Academy page; keep the dataset reference you recorded.

resetProcedure: Use the task's documented reset, not a manual drag of objects.
Confirm the follower and objects are back at the start state before engaging control again.
If a reset fails twice, end the episode as FAILURE with category reset-failure and note it.

failureTaxonomy.label: Gripper closed without holding the object
Object was held, then dropped before the goal
Follower or object hit the scene in a way that ended the attempt
Object reached the area but not the goal pose or region
Attempt ran past the time box you set
Input device tracking was lost or jumped
Control lag made the attempt uncontrollable
Scene did not return to its start state
Simulator physics or rendering became unstable
Operator stopped the attempt on purpose

episodeAcceptance: The episode was recorded through the official demonstration-recording path.
It has a label (SUCCESS, FAILURE or PARTIAL) and, unless SUCCESS, a failure category from this taxonomy.
It started from a confirmed reset state.
It is kept in the dataset even when it failed; exclusions are written in the session note with a reason.
recoveryProcedure: If control behaves unexpectedly, disengage first, then reset.
After a tracking-loss or input-lag failure, check the device before the next episode and note what you changed.
Count an episode as a recovery episode when you had to recover the object or scene mid-attempt.
replayChecklist: Play back at least one SUCCESS and one FAILURE episode if you have both.
Check that the label matches what happened in the replay.
Check that the failure category is the first thing that went wrong, not the last.
Note any episode whose replay does not match the recorded label, and fix the label before review.
